$description: Struct-level golden vectors for serializePruneEntry — the prune Merkle leaf preimage committed under subBlockRoot (TYPES_INTERFACE -> Layout - Stump / PruneEntry). Every field is fixed-width, so every writer throws outside its domain rather than sentinelling.

vectors.name: prune/author-two-ids
vectors.note: 226 bytes: 32 + (1 + 2x32) + 32 + 32 + 64 + 1. Every one of the six fields holds a DIFFERENT byte value, so a field-order error moves the bytes visibly instead of hiding inside a wall of repeats — the same reason the corpus README asks for distinct non-zero values in adjacent fields. Trailing 00 is enum8 trigger = author.

vectors.name: prune/storage-prune-empty-subtree
vectors.note: The other trigger tag, and the empty-array count. At 162 bytes this is the struct's floor, so it pins the shape the way post/minimal does — and the trailing 01 is the only non-zero byte, which makes the tag's position unmissable.

rejects.name: prune/unknown-trigger-tag
rejects.note: prune/author-two-ids with the trigger byte moved from 00 to 02. The tag table is CLOSED — reserving a retired value and refusing an unknown one are the same rule, and it is what makes an enum8 renumber a loud change rather than a silently moved Merkle root.

rejects.name: prune/non-minimal-subtree-count
rejects.note: The array's count written as the padded `82 00`. An ARRAY count rather than a scalar, deliberately: it is the least-watched integer in any layout and the one whose padding survives longest unnoticed.

rejects.name: prune/trailing-byte
rejects.note: One byte past a satisfied struct. This leaf is hashed into subBlockRoot, so slack here would be junk riding under a committed root.
